title: KKR Plans Over Rs 6,000 Crore Investment in PETRONAS Renewable Arm Gentari India
excerpt: The planned investment in Gentari Renewable India would give KKR an option to acquire a stake later, not equity now, The Economic Times reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
body:
• KKR plans to invest more than Rs 6,000 crore (about RM2.6 billion) in Gentari Renewable India, the Indian renewable energy arm of Malaysia's PETRONAS, The Economic Times reported on October 19, citing people familiar with the matter.
  • The investment would not give KKR an equity stake at this stage. KKR would instead hold an option to acquire a stake at a later date, according to the report.
  • Gentari Renewable India is seeking growth capital to expand its renewable energy and green hydrogen projects and to reduce debt.
  • For investors tracking India's energy transition: neither KKR, Gentari nor PETRONAS had confirmed the transaction in the reports published on October 19, and no closing timetable was disclosed — treat the deal as reported, not announced.

KKR plans to invest more than Rs 6,000 crore in Gentari Renewable India Pte Ltd, the renewable energy subsidiary of Malaysia's national oil company PETRONAS, according to The Edge Malaysia's report of The Economic Times story published on Monday, October 19. The Economic Times put the planned investment at over Rs 6,000 crore; The Edge Malaysia reported the same transaction at about RM2.6 billion.

How the Investment Is Structured

The capital injection will not translate into equity in Gentari Renewable India for KKR at this stage, The Economic Times reported, citing unidentified people familiar with the matter. Instead, KKR will have an option to acquire a stake in the company at a later date. That structure makes the transaction growth funding rather than an immediate change in ownership: PETRONAS retains control of Gentari Renewable India while KKR secures a path to equity if it chooses to exercise the option.

The reports did not disclose the instrument KKR would use, the size of the stake covered by the option, or any valuation for Gentari Renewable India. No statement from KKR, Gentari or PETRONAS confirming the terms accompanied the reporting.

Why Gentari Is Raising Capital

Gentari Renewable India has been looking to raise growth capital to fund the expansion of its renewable energy and green hydrogen projects and to lower its debt, The Economic Times said. The company has grown in part by acquisition. In March 2025, it acquired a 1.6-gigawatt solar and wind portfolio from Brookfield Asset Management for US$900 million (RM3.67 billion). In May 2024, the unit bought a 185-megawatt operating solar portfolio from Fortum Corporation and partners.

The company's own India business shows the base that new capital would build on. According to Gentari's India site, its distributed renewable business has more than 12 years of operating history across more than 1,000 sites nationwide, representing 2.1 gigawatts of installed capacity, including 650 megawatts of onsite solar installations. Its open access business operates 11 plants with over 1.5 GWp of combined solar and wind capacity. Gentari says it pioneered the Renewable Energy Service Company (RESCO) model for India's commercial and industrial segment, under which customers adopt renewable energy without upfront capital investment.

KKR's Existing India Renewables Exposure

KKR already invests in Indian clean energy. In its own release material, the firm lists Serentica Renewables, a clean-energy platform delivering power to large-scale industrial users in India, among its Asia Pacific energy transition platforms, alongside CleanPeak Energy and Zenith Energy in Australia. KKR says it has more than $100 billion in infrastructure assets under management and has invested more than $31 billion in energy transition and renewables infrastructure since 2011. A Gentari transaction would add a PETRONAS-backed utility-scale and distributed platform to that India exposure.

PETRONAS in India

PETRONAS, officially Petroliam Nasional Bhd, has built a presence in India through liquefied natural gas supplies, petrochemicals, petroleum trading and automotive lubricants, The Edge Malaysia reported. The Malaysian national oil company also holds a 50:50 joint venture with Indian Oil Corporation in liquefied petroleum gas. Gentari is the vehicle through which PETRONAS runs its clean energy business, covering renewable energy, hydrogen and green mobility.

What Happens Next

The next step is confirmation. Because the reporting rests on unidentified sources and no company statement has been published, the terms could change before any binding agreement. Investors should watch for a formal announcement from KKR or PETRONAS confirming the amount, the instrument and the conditions attached to KKR's option to acquire a stake, as well as any regulatory filings in India or Malaysia. Until then, the size of the cheque — more than Rs 6,000 crore — signals continued foreign private capital demand for Indian renewable platforms with operating portfolios and a green hydrogen pipeline.
